overview: Chips: TSMC is weighing a new multibillion-dollar Texas campus as AI chip demand stays extremely tight.
Big story: Anthropic is reportedly targeting a November IPO that could rival SpaceX's valuation.

items.headline: Microsoft's AI-driven quarter adds $1 trillion in market value
items.summary: Microsoft shares surged 37.5% from July to September, its best quarter in decades, adding roughly $1 trillion in market capitalization as Azure and Copilot demand stayed strong. The rally signals investors still back heavy AI capital spending despite broader cost concerns.

items.headline: Anthropic targets November IPO at a giant valuation
items.summary: Anthropic is reportedly targeting an IPO as soon as mid-November, with marketing potentially starting the week of November 9; the company was last valued near $965 billion in May. A listing of that scale would rank among the largest tech IPOs ever and test AI valuations.

items.headline: OpenAI launches 'Dots' agents, shelves GPT-6.1 Astra
items.summary: At DevDay, OpenAI introduced "Dots," always-on agents built on GPT-6 Astra that connect to apps including Slack and Microsoft Teams, while confirming it shelved a planned GPT-6.1 Astra update after internal testing found alignment failures. The move shows OpenAI pushing agentic products while tightening safety checks on its next flagship model.

items.headline: TSMC weighs new multibillion-dollar Texas chip campus
items.summary: TSMC is considering a new campus in Texas that could add tens of billions of dollars to its US expansion, on top of the $265 billion already committed to its Arizona site. The move reflects how tight AI chip capacity has become and the leverage Nvidia and Apple now hold over where their silicon is made.

items.headline: Stargate expands with five new AI data-center sites
items.summary: OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank said they are adding five new Stargate data-center locations, including sites in Shackelford County, Texas; Dona Ana County, New Mexico; and a new Midwest campus in Wisconsin. The expansion grows the companies' roughly $500 billion push to build out US AI compute capacity.

items.headline: Nvidia raises buyback authorization by $150 billion
items.summary: Nvidia's board approved a $150 billion increase to its share-repurchase program, lifting the total remaining authorization to $235 billion, the largest such increase in the company's history. The move signals confidence in Nvidia's cash generation even as AI-chip demand and capital spending both keep climbing.

items.headline: Google DeepMind shakes up leadership as Hassabis steps back
items.summary: Google DeepMind is restructuring its leadership: co-founder Demis Hassabis is stepping back from day-to-day management to become Chair of Google DeepMind and Alphabet's Chief Scientist, while Koray Kavukcuoglu steps up to oversee Gemini development and frontier research. The shift hands day-to-day model strategy to a new deputy as Google races rivals on AI.

items.headline: DeepSeek open-sources Huawei chip tools to rival Nvidia's CUDA
items.summary: DeepSeek released as open-source its chip-programming toolkit built with Huawei, including TileLang, positioned as a simpler alternative to Nvidia's CUDA software standard for Huawei's Ascend AI accelerators. The move could help Chinese developers wean off Nvidia hardware as US export controls squeeze access to advanced chips.

items.headline: Alibaba, ByteDance and Zhipu AI named on Time's AI list
items.summary: Alibaba, ByteDance and Zhipu AI were named among Time magazine's first list of the most influential AI companies, reflecting their rapid rise through open-source models and consumer-facing apps. Alibaba and Zhipu have driven adoption via open models while ByteDance scaled consumer apps like Doubao, underscoring China's deepening presence in frontier AI.

items.headline: Huang: AI distillation is 'competition,' not 'theft'
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC that AI model distillation is simply "competition," pushing back after the White House and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent branded the practice "theft." The exchange highlights friction over how Washington should treat Chinese AI firms that build on US model outputs.

items.headline: Su: AI chip demand shows no sign of slowing
items.summary: AMD CEO Lisa Su said demand for AI computing is not slowing "at all," pointing to sustained hyperscaler spending as a reason for optimism about the company's growth. Her comments reinforce the view that the current AI infrastructure buildout still has room to run despite valuation worries.

items.headline: Huang emerges as Trump administration's top AI-safety ally
items.summary: CNBC reported that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has emerged as the Trump administration's leading industry voice in the debate over AI safety, as the White House and AI labs spar over how fast development should proceed. Huang's alignment with Washington puts Nvidia at the center of the fight over US AI policy.

items.headline: EU agrees to simplify AI Act, ban 'nudification' apps
items.summary: The European Commission said EU lawmakers agreed to simplify parts of the AI Act to ease compliance burdens on businesses, while banning "nudification" apps that generate non-consensual sexual images. The deal balances industry pressure to cut red tape against new protections for citizens from AI-enabled abuse.

items.headline: UK minister: Britain needs more control and leverage over AI
items.summary: The UK government said Britain must secure greater control and leverage over AI to protect its national security in an increasingly fractured world, signaling a shift toward treating AI capability as a strategic asset. The statement underscores London's push to build sovereign AI capacity rather than depend solely on US or Chinese technology.

items.headline: UK backs AI drug-discovery and cheap-compute startups
items.summary: The UK government announced its first round of backing under the Sovereign AI program for firms working on drug discovery, cheaper supercomputing and related technology. The funding is meant to grow homegrown AI hardware and research capacity as Britain competes for a bigger share of the global AI industry.

items.headline: China proposes global AI governance body, WAICO
items.summary: Chinese officials have floated creating a World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, or WAICO, to coordinate AI rules across countries, as Beijing pushes rapid, incremental AI regulation at home. The proposal positions China as an alternative rule-setter to the US-led approach to global AI governance.

items.headline: IndiaAI Mission scales up to 38,000 GPUs under Rs 10,300 crore plan
items.summary: India's government said its IndiaAI Mission is scaling up toward 38,000 GPUs under a Rs 10,300 crore ($1.2 billion) national compute program. The build-out is meant to give Indian startups, researchers and government agencies subsidised access to AI computing as the country pushes its own domestic AI strategy.

items.headline: India must keep its AI push going despite global slowdown calls
items.summary: Business Standard reported that India needs to maintain momentum on AI development even as some global voices call for a slowdown, arguing a pause would leave the country further behind the US and China. The piece frames India's compute and talent investments as too early-stage to pause.
